title: Sustaining Intangible Cultural Practices in Contexts of Forced Displacement
content:
Blue Shield International is pleased to announce its patronage of the international research project 

World Universities Network “Research Development Fund” project.

Project Leader: A/Prof Catherine Grant, Griffith University, Australia

As 2025 began, over 123 million people were forcibly displaced globally—a figure that has risen each year since 2015, and that risks growing further amid intersecting global geopolitical and environmental crises.

Cultural losses incurred through displacement exacerbate the challenges of those processes for individuals and communities, and impede international efforts to urgently safeguard at-risk intangible cultural practices.

For people experiencing forced displacement, intangible cultural practices of the homeland can powerfully promote psychosocial wellbeing and social connection, due to their strong links with cultural identity and collective memory. The world over, however, displaced people encounter major impediments to sustaining and transmitting their intangible cultural practices.
